Track a VRM avatar’s face, body and fingers

Set up webcam tracking for a VRM avatar in V Lens. Explore body and finger tracking, hand stability settings, and landmark previews.

The app interface is currently in Japanese. The instructions below include the Japanese menu and control labels.

To try a model before preparing your own VRM, open File (ファイル) → Built-in samples (内蔵サンプル) → Sendagaya Shino (VRM) (千駄ヶ谷 篠（VRM）).

Connect a VRM avatar to your webcam

In 0.1.76, the right-hand Output tab (出力) for PSD and VRM avatars has a switch below the expression selector to turn camera tracking on or off directly. It applies and saves the change immediately while stopped or during output. Click Camera tracking settings… (カメラトラッキング設定…) for detailed settings. Settings (設定) → Camera tracking… (カメラトラッキング…) remains available.

Changes in the settings dialog apply immediately, without an Apply and save button (適用して保存). Applied settings are saved when you close the dialog and when the app exits. If a change fails, the controls return to the actual settings and show an error. If saving fails, the dialog stays open so you can retry.

  1. Load a VRM 0.x or VRM 1.0 file with Open model… (モデルを開く…).
  2. Stop output, open Settings (設定) → Camera tracking… (カメラトラッキング…), and choose your webcam. Turn on Link face and body to camera (顔・身体をカメラに連動).
  3. Click Start preview (プレビュー開始), face forward, and choose Use current orientation as reference (現在の向きを基準にする). Check head movement and blinking, close the settings dialog, then start output.

Switch avatars and tracking during output

In 0.1.73, you can switch models and built-in samples while outputting a PSD or VRM. Configured PSDs can also be loaded through their saved settings JSON. The output connection and format stay in use; if preparation fails, the previous avatar continues. PSD switching and layer assignment requirements

Open Settings (設定) → Camera tracking (カメラトラッキング…) to change the tracking toggle or lip-sync input source immediately during output. If enabling tracking fails, the previous setting remains. Turning tracking off from Camera only (カメラのみ) first prepares the audio input for lip sync. Stop output to change the camera, angle limits, movement mapping, body mode, hand stability or CPU/GPU selection.

Adjust head movement, gaze and lip sync

Head movement, gaze and blinking are applied to the bones and expressions supported by the model. For movement that behaves like a mirror, choose Mirror (鏡) under Movement mapping (動きの対応) in the camera tracking settings.

Lip sync has five blend positions, from Audio only (音声のみ) to Camera only (カメラのみ). You can use your microphone for the mouth while using the webcam for blinking and head movement. Choose Natural face and upper-body movement (顔＋上半身の自然な連動) to let the neck and shoulders follow along.

Use body and finger tracking

Stop output and open the camera tracking settings. Choose a mode under VRM body (VRMの身体); the selection applies immediately.

  • Face only (顔のみ) — Links head orientation, blinking and lip sync.
  • Natural face and upper-body movement (default) (顔＋上半身の自然な連動) — Lets the neck, chest and shoulders follow head movement gently.
  • Full-body and finger tracking (全身・手指トラッキング) — Tracks body orientation, arms and legs, palms and wrists, and individual fingers on both hands. The model needs the corresponding bones.

For full-body movement, keep your head and feet in the frame and make sure your hands are large enough for the fingers to be visible. When the camera supports it, full-body mode uses input close to 720p and crops around the hands for finger detection. Head movement is processed separately from body and hand tracking. Speed and accuracy depend on your camera, PC, lighting and how large your hands appear.

Move body and hand processing to the GPU

Full-body mode includes Body and hand processing (身体・手の処理). CPU is the default. To try GPU processing, stop output and choose Reduce CPU load with the GPU (GPUでCPU負荷を軽減); the change applies immediately. The preview uses your selected setting and shows whether the CPU or GPU is actually in use. Tracking continues on the CPU if the GPU is unavailable or processing fails.

Face tracking continues independently on the CPU. The GPU and CPU modes use different models, so their movements may differ. Results depend on the GPU, its driver, and other apps such as OBS or games sharing it.

Reduce false hand detections

In full-body mode, Hand tracking (手の追跡) lets you choose between faster response and more stable detection. Stop output before changing it; the selection applies immediately.

  • Fast response (反応優先) — Applies hand movement without an extra confirmation wait.
  • Balanced (default) (バランス) — Confirms the same hand in two consecutive frames before applying it. At 30 FPS input, the extra confirmation wait is about 33 ms.
  • Stability first (安定優先) — Confirms the hand across four consecutive frames. At 30 FPS input, it allows about 100 ms of extra confirmation wait to reduce brief false detections.

These are approximate extra waits when a hand is newly detected or its position or orientation changes sharply. A continuously tracked hand does not receive the same fixed delay on every update. Face tracking is unaffected.

When an elbow or hand is hidden

If the shoulder and wrist remain visible while the elbow is hidden, V Lens estimates the elbow using wrist motion and palm orientation. When an arm’s position or rotation is uncertain, it favors a relaxed A-pose with the arm slightly lowered. Forearm twist and wrist tilt are handled separately to reduce abrupt flips and unnatural bends. Shoulder angles are constrained to keep the upper arm and forearm in front of the torso when reaching across the body. This uses an approximate body boundary, so contact can remain with some model shapes or thick clothing.

During a brief tracking loss, the previous pose is held. If the loss continues, the arm and fingers gradually return to a relaxed pose. A single camera cannot accurately recover the position and rotation of every hidden joint; overlap and movement outside the frame can still cause errors.

Check face, body and finger detections

Choose Start preview (プレビュー開始) → Mosaic video + landmarks (モザイク映像＋ランドマーク). In full-body mode, the face landmarks are joined by a blue body skeleton, orange left-hand joints and purple right-hand joints. Left and right refer to the person in front of the camera. Detected hands are also displayed when the face or body is not visible.

Changing the camera, body mode, hand stability or processing device during a preview restarts it with the new settings. You can change angle limits and movement mapping without stopping the preview.

3D face (顔の3D) is a face-only 3D view. Raw camera video is not displayed. The mosaic view overlays detections from the same captured camera frame.

If the face is not detected or the forward direction drifts

Keep your entire face in the camera’s view and check the landmarks. Once your face is detected, choose Use current orientation as reference (現在の向きを基準にする) while facing forward comfortably. During output, you can also use Recenter (正面合わせ) on the monitor. If head movement is too large, stop output and reduce the angle limits.

GLB and FBX models can also be loaded. Supported movements depend on the model’s skeleton and expression data. For a PSD avatar, camera tracking can tilt the flat image and drive its eye layers.
